Project proposal

Xintong Xu

2026-11-16

Source: vignettes/proposal.qmd

To: BST260 Teaching Team, Fall 2026

This project will present two separate analyses: BMI and systolic blood pressure in NHANES, and food-preparation setting and reported foodborne outbreak size in CDC surveillance data. Each analysis will have its own vignette. The datasets represent different populations and will not be merged.

1. BMI and systolic blood pressure

Question: Among adults aged 40 years or older in the 2009–2012 NHANES data, how is BMI associated with average systolic blood pressure?

Data and variables

I will use NHANESraw from the R package NHANES (version 2.1.4), containing 20,293 participants from the 2009–2010 and 2011–2012 cycles. Each observation represents one participant. This object retains survey-design variables and differs from the package’s resampled NHANES object. These packaged data are intended for educational use.

The exposure is BMI in kg/m², modeled continuously and reported per 5-unit increase. The outcome is BPSysAve, average systolic blood pressure in mmHg, a continuous variable. The target population is adults aged 40+ in the civilian, noninstitutionalized US population covered by NHANES, although missing data and the educational extract limit population inference.

Before fitting models, I specify adjustment for age, sex, race/ethnicity (Race1), education, family income-to-poverty ratio (Poverty), and survey cycle. Age and sex relate to both body composition and blood pressure. Socioeconomic circumstances and social conditions can influence both outcomes; race/ethnicity will be treated as a social-context variable, not a biological explanation. Cycle accounts for differences between survey periods. Age and income-to-poverty ratio will initially be continuous; other covariates will be categorical.

Feasibility and analysis

The extract contains 7,738 adults aged 40+, with 7,060 having both BMI and blood pressure observed. BMI is missing for 391, blood pressure for 581, education for 17, and income-to-poverty ratio for 790. There are 6,392 participants with all primary-model variables observed and positive examination weights.

I will describe missingness and participant characteristics, plot BMI against blood pressure, and fit survey-weighted linear regression. I will construct the design using strata (SDMVSTRA), clusters (SDMVPSU), and four-year examination weights (WTMEC2YR / 2). I will define the design on participants with positive examination weights before subsetting to the analysis domain. Results will include adjusted differences in mmHg and 95% confidence intervals.

The primary analysis will use complete cases. I will compare included and excluded participants and examine sensitivity to omitting the income variable, including a comparison on the same sample. Residual plots and a nonlinear BMI term will assess model form. Survey weights do not automatically correct item nonresponse. Cross-sectional measurement, unavailable treatment information, unmeasured confounding, and age top-coding at 80 limit interpretation. Results will describe associations, not causal effects.

2. Setting and reported foodborne outbreak size

Question: Among reported single-state foodborne outbreaks during 2009–2023, does the mean reported number of illnesses differ between restaurant and private-home food-preparation settings?

Data and variables

I will use the CDC outbreak extract supplied as waterborne in finalproject. Despite its name, it includes several transmission modes. Each observation is one reported outbreak. I will select primary_mode == "Food" and years 2009–2023, beginning with the NORS reporting era and ending with the last year in this extract. I will retain outbreaks assigned to one of the 50 states or the District of Columbia and exclude multistate and territorial records.

The exposure is food-preparation setting, coded as restaurant versus private home, with private home as the reference. Restaurant categories begin with Restaurant:. Home categories are Private home/residence, Residence - Single-family home, and Residence - Multi-unit housing. Semicolon-separated settings will be retained only if all entries belong to the same exposure group. Other, mixed, unknown, and missing settings will be excluded from the primary comparison and counted in an exclusion summary. The outcome is illnesses, a count of reported cases within an outbreak.

Feasibility and analysis

There are 11,358 foodborne outbreaks in 2009–2023. Applying the setting and geographic restrictions leaves 6,763 outbreaks: 5,836 restaurant and 927 private-home outbreaks. Illness counts and months are observed in this subset.

I will summarize counts, medians, and distributions by setting, then fit a log-link quasi-Poisson model to allow variance greater than the mean. The primary adjustment variables will be calendar year, season derived from month, and state, all categorical, to account for temporal, seasonal, geographic, and reporting differences. These variables are specified before estimating the setting association. I will report an adjusted mean count ratio and 95% confidence interval, with dispersion and influence checks.

Etiology is missing for 1,722 eligible outbreaks. A sensitivity analysis among the remaining 5,041 will add prespecified etiology groups: norovirus, Salmonella, other single etiologies, and multiple etiologies. Missing etiology will not be interpreted as absence of a pathogen. I will also examine whether the association changes when restricting to 2009–2019.

Voluntary reporting, incomplete ascertainment, pathogen information, and the number of people served may differ by setting. These data contain outbreaks, not all meals or exposed people. Therefore, the comparison cannot estimate the risk of becoming ill after eating at a restaurant versus at home.

Deliverables

I will create separate NHANES and outbreak vignettes with provenance, descriptive tables, plots, methods, findings, and limitations. Provenance will document the original data producer, source links, data periods, package or snapshot versions, access dates, and all selection and cleaning steps. Descriptive tables will include sample sizes, missingness, means and standard deviations, medians and interquartile ranges, and category counts and percentages as appropriate. I will validate the R package with R CMD check, resolve relevant issues, rebuild the pkgdown site, and publish the package source on GitHub and the rendered vignettes on GitHub Pages. Reusable R functions will summarize missingness and convert the outbreak list into a validated analysis table with documented setting categories. The package website title will remain BST260 final project. I will confirm the proposed NHANES question with the teaching team if it requires approval as a custom question.
